decisions.reason: Having survived its first year and fitting very closely with the firm's integrated airport-operations core, it is likely meeting or remaining close enough to aspiration levels that management keeps it while scaling adoption.

As a module that builds directly on established apron integration capabilities, it is likely to be retained because no clear performance shortfall is visible and the growing firm has slack to continue learning.

This software is the least central to the firm's core operational-control identity, so after another year management would scrutinize it more against aspiration levels, but in the absence of clear failure it would still more likely be kept than dropped.

Because it supports the firm's move toward data-driven monitoring and lifecycle services and can leverage the installed base, management would likely continue it unless results clearly fall below expectations.

Its close relation to apron coordination and resource optimization makes it complementary to the firm's main offer, so boundedly rational management would usually keep it while exploiting cross-selling and service ties.

A controller safety alert service is highly aligned with the firm's safety-focused value proposition and customer base, so continued retention is likely unless performance is markedly below aspiration levels.
